stories.title: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk"): 1T-parameter natively multimodal MoE in public preview, open weights expected end of October
stories.summary: Mistral shipped Mistral Large 4 into public-preview API: a 1T-parameter natively multimodal mixture-of-experts with 49B active parameters, positioned as the strongest US/EU open-weight model on their aggregate, with vendor-reported cyber (82% on an Artificial Analysis reproduction task, 93% on Cybench), finance, legal and visual-grounding results. Preview pricing is $1.36/$4.18 per million input/output tokens. Caveat: weights are not out - architecture and post-training details are deferred, and the cyber comparisons are partly against closed models that refuse the task.

source.name: Mistral AI official X post (2026-10-06 13:06 UTC)

quality.note: Official vendor post plus official release page; benchmarks are vendor-reported.

stories.title: Claude lands in Google Docs, Sheets and Slides: in-place edits with approval cards, public beta on paid plans
stories.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude as a Workspace sidebar that reads the open file and edits in place with approval cards by default, plus separate Docs/Sheets/Slides connectors that create and edit those files from chat - public beta on all paid plans, with access following existing Google permissions. For builders, in-place doc editing with a permission model that inherits Google's ACLs is the concrete pattern to watch. Caveat: beta, paid plans only; Team/Enterprise owners must enable connectors; no new model is involved.

stories.title: OpenAI publishes new math results from an unnamed internal frontier model, with Lean formalizations in open repo
stories.summary: OpenAI released writeups of new math results from an unnamed internal frontier model, published after consultation with the IAS Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI, with reasoning summaries, attempt statistics, and Lean formalizations in an open GitHub repo. Caveat: the model is not released and the post does not name the problems; Sam Altman's post links the same URL, not a second result.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Cyber Verification Program: three vetted access tiers for Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 with fewer cyber blocks
stories.summary: Anthropic opened a Cyber Verification Program with three verified tiers - Defense, Red Team (authorized pentesting) and Specialized - for Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, with fewer cyber blocks than public models, available on Claude Platform, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry. Their CyScenarioBench check: public Opus 5.5 blocked every task on the first prompt; Defense tier blocked 46/50 trials; Red Team blocked none and finished 34/50. Caveat: enrollment is application-only, use requires data retention with narrow zero-retention exceptions, and Bedrock is only for Enterprise Frontier Safeguards customers.

stories.title: Google releases EmbeddingGemma 2: 740M-param open multimodal embedding model (Apache 2.0), one space for text, code, image, audio and video
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released EmbeddingGemma 2 under Apache 2.0: a 740M-parameter on-device embedding model with one vector space for text, code, images, audio and video; the text-only path drops to ~270M, vectors are Matryoshka-truncatable from 768 to 128 dimensions, with 8K context. Weights are on Hugging Face and Kaggle. Caveat: 'best-in-class' is their sub-1B comparison, and the full multimodal footprint is larger than the 740M headline once optional vision/audio encoders are added.

stories.title: OpenAI opens public beta of the Decisions API: POST /v1/decisions on gpt-6-luna for classification, choice and scoring up to 10x faster than Responses
stories.summary: OpenAI's Decisions API entered public beta on gpt-6-luna only: a single endpoint accepting text and inline images that returns a predicate probability, a choice from a fixed set, or a score on ordered levels. OpenAI says it is up to 10x faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API, and docs price it at $0.10 per million input tokens with no output tokens charged. Caveat: beta with GA expected in coming weeks; hosted image URLs and file_id are not accepted, and the speed claim is versus the Responses API, not an independent baseline.

stories.title: US Treasury's FinCEN withdraws two crypto surveillance proposals: self-custody wallet reporting and international mixing
stories.summary: FinCEN scrapped a 2020 proposal that would have required banks and money service businesses to report crypto transactions above $10,000 involving unhosted (self-custody) wallets, and a 2023 proposal to impose a special reporting measure on international crypto mixing (pooling, splitting transfers, single-use wallets). For builders, this removes a heavy KYC/reporting burden on self-custody flows and mixer operators - FinCEN cited chilling effects on legitimate activity. Caveat: FinCEN says it will keep monitoring mixers, and no Federal Register link was posted - the withdrawal is confirmed via CoinDesk's official account, not yet a Treasury document.

source.name: CoinDesk official X post (2026-10-05 18:00 UTC)

quality.note: Official newsroom account post plus detailed second-outlet article; official Treasury document not yet linked.

stories.title: Bank of Russia opens application registers for cryptocurrency exchanges and custodians under 282-FZ
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia has opened applications for exchange and custodian registers under Federal Law 282-FZ (in force since Sept 1, 2026): exchanges need 15 million rubles in own funds, primary and backup facilities inside Russia, and face a 30-working-day review; non-qualified investors are capped at 300,000 rubles of crypto purchases per year. For builders, this puts a formal supervised exchange regime with a concrete application route in place in Russia. Caveat: opening the window is not automatic admission - each applicant gets an individual decision; the CBR's own implementing notice was published Sept 24.

source.name: CoinDesk official X post (2026-10-05 17:18 UTC)

quality.note: Official newsroom account post plus second-outlet article with the CBR rule detail; no direct CBR link in the post.

stories.title: Science Advances: cross-national 'speech clock' tracks biological aging and dementia markers in Latin American populations
stories.summary: A Science Advances paper ('Speech clocks decode dementia phenotypes, social exposome, and biological aging', DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aef9864, online 2026-09-30; in print Oct 2, Vol 12, Issue 40) develops a cross-national speech clock that tracks biological aging and dementia markers in Latin American populations. For longevity-biomarker builders, language-based proxies for physiological aging are cheap, scalable signals worth benchmarking. Caveat: a measurement paper, not a treatment; the journal's social push (Oct 6) is nine days after online publication, so this is a catch-up inclusion.

stories.title: Science policy forum: aging/longevity products should go through existing FDA approval routes, with effectiveness and safety evidence
stories.summary: A Science Policy Forum ('Longevity products: Innovation through regulation', Strassle, Fernandez Lynch and Zettler; Science 394(6819):33-35, published online Oct 1) argues that products claiming to prevent or reverse aging should enter through existing FDA approval routes and need evidence of effectiveness and safety - a regulatory roadmap for the longevity-drug pipeline. For longevity-tech builders, it frames the likely regulatory posture for aging-biomarker claims. Caveat: analysis/policy, not new science; the article published online 2026-10-01, so this is a catch-up inclusion on Science's Oct 6 push of it (post has no URL - title/DOI recovered from the indexed post).
